doc.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007

title: Europe after 9/11 and teaching in Graz
summary: He recalls colleagues in Europe in late 2001 questioning CNN, feeling respected as a musician there, and getting the Graz teaching job through Mark Murphy.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: This is exactly what I wrote it for. I was in Europe. I went to Europe at the end of September in 2001, and I got there and my colleagues were saying, “Is CNN part of government?”

Part of the U.S. — they were asking because they had taken up the line of the Bush administration about, you know, we have to go to war. They had hook, line and sinker become part of his thrust. And they were wondering what’s going on. How come the BBC is the only thing that they were getting good information from. Yeah. And one other thing, when you said going to Europe to record that album with the orchestra. You know I came back from Europe and people would say, “Well how was it.” I said, “Well in the United States I’m a degenerate jazz musician. There, I have colleagues.”
And that’s how it felt. It was wonderful there. I had a classical teacher teaching under my chair. It was unbelievable. So that’s another difference that I would like to point out.
Did you tell me, again, where you were teaching?
I was teaching at KUG Graz.
Kunst University Graz in Graz, Austria.
Wow. How did you get a gig like that?

Mark Murphy again. Mark Murphy has been a wonderful friend and I love the way he sings and I’m happy to say he likes the way I sing. So actually Nancy King, a great singer from Portland, Oregon was supposed to do it and she broke her leg. So it’s like, “Break a leg, Nancy.” Literally.
And so I got the gig.
